newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bonds to consolidate if RBA stays quiet.
newsitem.headline: Australian bonds to consolidate if RBA stays quiet.

text.p: *Australian bonds look set for a day of consolidation after Thursday's steamy rally should the Reserve Bank make no announcement on monetary policy this morning.

Australian bonds look set for a day of consolidation after Thursday's steamy rally should the Reserve Bank make no announcement on monetary policy this morning, which many see as the most likely case.
Thursday's disappointing employment report refuelled hopes of a further easing in monetary policy with a 50 basis points reduction fully factored in across the yield curve.
Ten-year bond yields have backed up slightly since dropping to fresh 3-1/2 year lows of below 6.60 percent on the data, although still remain some 15 basis points below levels seen late on Monday.

"I think it's a day of consolidation. We saw little profit-taking from the offshore overnight, and I think the domestics did all they needed to do on Thursday and squared up ahead of the U.S. PPI tonight," one trader said.

September bill futures were easier after striking a contract high of 94.99 on Thursday, but were still more or less pricing in a 50 basis point easing in current official 5.5 percent interest rates after inflation and wages data later this month.
May housing finance is due at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT). Median forecasts centre on a 5.7 percent fall after the 12.2 percent rise in April, according to a Reuters survey of economists.

The local market slightly underperformed the U.S., which held little changed on Thursday ahead of the PPI later on Tuesday. The Australian/U.S. 10-year bond yield spread sank to its lowest level in well over decade at around 35 basis points on Thursday following the jobs data.
